query: How does CPython's dict implementation probe for a free slot and resize its hash table when it grows?

matches.reason: Implements the open-addressing perturbation probe sequence (hash & mask, then perturb-based rehashing) used to locate a free slot for a new key.
Wrapper that triggers a table resize (growth) when insertion runs out of usable slots, computing the new size via GROWTH_RATE.
Core resize routine: allocates a new larger keys table and rehashes/reinserts all existing entries into it, implementing dict growth.
